title: Closed subgroup representing the adjoint stabilizer of a Lie element
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G,C$ be $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, using the canonical Lie algebra and its tangent point $t_X\in G(k[\epsilon])$ [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation]. A homomorphism $j:C\to G$ represents the Lie-element centralizer if it is a closed subgroup inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] and, for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, its image on $R$-points consists exactly of the points $g\in G(R)$ whose constant lift to $G(R[\epsilon])$ commutes with the image of $t_X$ under $k[\epsilon]\to R[\epsilon]$. Here $R[\epsilon]$ denotes the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers], the constant lift is $R\to R[\epsilon]$, and $k[\epsilon]\to R[\epsilon]$ is the $k$-algebra map $a+b\epsilon\mapsto a+b\epsilon$ given by the universal property of the dual numbers. By the conjugation characterization of the adjoint action (proved separately, not part of this definition), the condition is equivalently $\operatorname{Ad}(g)(1\otimes X)=1\otimes X$. All test algebras, including nonreduced ones and the zero algebra, are included.

source.place: Proposition 17.76, printed p.377, and Section 10.19, pp.191–192: the adjoint stabilizer described through conjugation of the canonical infinitesimal point.
